narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outlook, in order of importance, were your total years of professional experience, the length of time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter careers (1–5 years is most common among stayers), your mid-range experience level signals to the model a greater likelihood of exploring new opportunities elsewhere. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your present organization also contributed toward predicting departure. This tenure is actually the most frequent range among those expected to stay, yet in your specific combination of factors it still leaned the outcome toward leaving. Finally, the fact that you have received other job offers during your time here was another notable push in the same direction. Most employees the model expects to stay have not received such external opportunities.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization sees you as someone with enough experience and external interest to potentially move on. You and your manager should discuss ways to strengthen your sense of long-term fit and growth within the company, such as clearer career paths or additional responsibilities that align with your experience. Addressing these areas could help shift future assessments. (248 words)
